facts.F1: Story 6368 S04b: reduce Models to the shared kernel and add a kernel-size rule. Every type under Lighthouse.Backend.Models is either the shared kernel ADR-270 Decision 7 allows (IDomainEvent, IEntity, IConcurrencyTokenEntity) or owned by a named context with a blocker measured from the compiled code and the Story that frees it; the free ones move to their owner (Platform/<Area> or Modules/<Owner>/{Domain,Application}); a rule keeps that catalogue true and shrinking. Behaviour-free. Design: docs/feature/story-6368-s04b-models-to-kernel/feature-delta.md (its slice S4, the event move, is already done by Story 6382 and is dropped; its S5 is this feature's S4).
facts.F10: Every Models type has a known owner and a true reason to stay.
facts.F11: The Platform-owned free files move to Platform/<Area>; their catalogue rows name the new namespace.
facts.F12: The platform lane holds its own types.
facts.F13: The context-owned free files move to Modules/<Owner>/Domain or Application with their unit tests; their catalogue rows name the new namespace.
facts.F14: Each context holds its own types.
facts.F15: The rules name moved types by namespace only (movers list empty), a planted Models type off the catalogue fails naming itself, and ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 and ADR-270 D7 describe the kernel.
facts.F16: A new type in Models cannot land unseen.
facts.F2: A maintainer sees for every Models type who owns it and why it still sits there, and a new context type placed in Models fails the architecture rules and names itself.
facts.F3: Every type in Lighthouse.Backend.Models is on one catalogue, closed both ways: it stands as Kernel (one of the three base types ADR-270 Decision 7 allows) or as owned by a named context with a blocker that is true when measured from the compiled code and the EF model, and the Story that frees it.
facts.F4: The Models types that nothing blocks leave Models: Platform-owned ones to Platform/<Area>, context-owned ones to Modules/<Owner>/Domain or Application, with their unit tests beside them, and every module's boundary and placement rules still green.
facts.F5: A type added to Models that is not on the catalogue, or a catalogue row whose claim is false, fails the architecture rules and names itself and the fix; the rules name the moved types by their new namespace only, with no old-path allowance left.
facts.F6: Nothing a user or a client sees changes: no schema, migration, route, DTO, payload, usage-data event or answer differs from the revision before the Story.
facts.F7: ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 and ADR-270 Decision 7 describe the kernel as it is after the Story and point to the catalogue for every other Models type.
facts.F8: Moving EF entities, wire types (DTOs and controller signatures) or types held by a staying Models type; splitting files of mixed standing; moving event types (done by Story 6382); any schema or behaviour change.
facts.F9: The catalogue: one row per Models type with its standing (Kernel or owner and measured blocker), the movers named with old and new namespace, and the move law sees the Models map; red today for the movers.
